digest.component_or_area: dependency advisory gate and CI/release pipeline
propositions: A committed uv lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any newly-published advisory against a pinned version to block CI/release gating for all in-flight changes regardless of whether they touch that dependency.

The current pip-audit job applies the same gating rule to all changes; the specification splits gating by lane: Gerrit verify blocks only when the change touches the dependency map, while scheduled main blocks only releases, fixing the six-changes-one-incident problem.

Developers misunderstand constraint-dependencies vs override-dependencies: constraint-dependencies can only narrow and returns UNSATISFIABLE as its expected output (not proof of impossibility); override-dependencies is the correct instrument to patch around an upstream cap.

The gate must distinguish real advisories from database-unreachable flakes and must not allow recheck to clear a real finding; a runbook and escalation mechanism (dependency-advisory-canary.yml) are required to route triage to the lock owner.

Severity enrichment from OSV is needed because pip-audit does not carry severity; the specification adopts the OSS bar (CRITICAL/HIGH fail, MEDIUM warns, LOW tracked) with unrated advisories treated as HIGH and failing.

Override-dependencies remedies require a REMOVE-WHEN justification naming the advisory, capping package, and safety argument, with verification set (uv lock --check, uv sync --locked --extra dev, pip-audit on full environment) to confirm the old pin masked no other vulnerabilities.
